title: DeskGrantConstraintsV1
description: The limits on a grant to administer desks: `api.write` on `apis/desks`. Exactly one of two closed forms. FULL (`#/$defs/full`): the organization's own desks grant, every limit written out. FOLLOW (`#/$defs/follow`): an agent's grant that carries no limits of its own and follows the organization's desks grant on the same gate, so there is no copied limits file and no end time typed by hand to drift from it. Govern resolves a follow form into that grant's limits at token time. A document that mixes the two forms is refused: a follow form that also carries a limit is a second source of limits.

full.description: The limits written out. They are stored on the grant, copied by Govern into the signed gate token's `constraints`, and enforced by the backend adapter before any backend call. CLOSED: an unknown key is refused, never ignored, because an ignored limit is a limit nobody enforces. Every list the adapter needs in order to allow anything is required and non-empty: no list, no create. Rules a schema cannot state are the adapter's, and refuse with the code naming the limit: every name in `providers` has an entry in `provider_config_digests`, and no other name does; a create's image digest (after `@`, or the whole value when it is a local content ID) is in `image_digests`; every host in `policy_baseline.network.allowed_hosts` is inside the `allowed_hosts` ceiling; a create's CPU and memory limit is at most `resources`, and a grant without `resources` allows no create.

image_digests.description: The images a desk may be created from, by digest: a registry digest for an image from a registry, or the local content ID (Docker's image ID) for an image the machine built itself. They are different hashes of one image; list the one the create names. A create whose image digest is not here is refused CONSTRAINT_IMAGE_DIGESTS.

policy_digests.description: The reviewed BASELINE policies a create may start from, by the digest the adapter computes. They govern a create only; later changes are held to `allowed_hosts`.

allowed_hosts.description: The ceiling: every host any desk policy allows, at create and after every later change, must be one of these, or under a `*.` entry. A change that reaches outside it is refused CONSTRAINT_ALLOWED_HOSTS.

providers.description: The providers a desk may have attached. Empty means none.

provider_config_digests.description: For each provider, the digest of the configuration the Enclave accepted at install. An attach or detach of a provider whose configuration no longer matches is refused CONSTRAINT_PROVIDER_CONFIG_DIGESTS.

environment_keys.description: The environment names a create may set. Empty means none.

repo_hosts.description: Unused since 0.65.0: a create carries no repository (repositories reach a desk through a setup plan), so nothing reads this limit. It stays required so every grant written before stays valid; write [].

policy_baseline.description: What every desk policy, at create and after every change, must keep. The adapter compares the RESULTING policy with it, not only the request.

must_equal.description: The parts of a policy that may never differ from the baseline a desk started from: filesystem access, process identity, user namespaces, enforcement mode, and driver and runtime settings. All six, always: leaving one out would let a change reach it.

allowed_hosts.description: The hosts the baseline policy itself allows. Each is inside the `allowed_hosts` ceiling.

allowed_ports.description: The only ports any network rule may name, for example 443 and 22.

allowed_cidrs.description: Address ranges a network rule may name. Empty means none: a rule names hosts. Up to 64, so a discovery window can name the public IPv4 internet as ranges that leave out loopback, link-local, private and multicast space (51 of them; NVIDIA OpenShell refuses 0.0.0.0/0 as one range).

provider_added.description: A change may add the network access a provider needs only for a provider in `providers`.

resources.description: The most CPU and memory one desk may be created with: a create's `resources` must be at most each value. OPTIONAL in this schema only so that a grant written before it stays valid for every other change; a create needs it, and the adapter refuses every create under a grant without it. Either refusal is CONSTRAINT_RESOURCES.

max_cpu_millicores.description: Thousandths of one CPU, as a create's `cpu_millicores`.

discovery.description: OPTIONAL: an open discovery window, written by the installer for a limited time. Absent means no desk may enter auto approval mode. The adapter allows `approval_mode` `auto` only for a desk whose name starts with `name_prefix`, whose image digest is in `image_digests`, and whose every attached provider is in `providers`, else it refuses DESK_NOT_DISCOVERY; after `expires_at` it refuses DISCOVERY_WINDOW_CLOSED. It widens nothing else: a create is still held to every other limit here.

image_digests.description: The images a discovery desk may be created from, by digest.

providers.description: The only providers a discovery desk may have attached. Empty means none.

name_prefix.description: Every discovery desk's name starts with it, so an ordinary desk can never be one.

expires_at.description: When the window closes, UTC. A permit never outlives it.

projects.description: OPTIONAL: the server's own projects, each a team's desk image and its own reviewed policy. Absent or empty means none. A project widens nothing by itself: its `image_id` must also be in `image_digests` and its `policy_digest` in `policy_digests`, and every reader refuses a grant where either is missing. A schema cannot state that rule. Two entries never share a name.

name.description: The project's name on this server.

image_id.description: The project's desk image: the local content ID of an image built on the server.

policy_digest.description: The digest the adapter computes for the project's own policy.

since.description: When the project entered the grant, UTC, to the second. A reader also parses it as a real calendar time and refuses one that is not (for example 30 February).

requires_role.description: The organization role a run must have been started by for Govern to sign a token from this grant. Govern checks it when the grant is used; the adapter does not.

follow.description: Follow the organization's own desks grant on this gate, and carry no limits of its own. CLOSED and exactly two keys: any limit beside `follow` (an `image_digests`, a `discovery` window) is refused, because a follow form is one source of limits, never a copy beside it.

grant.description: The grant followed: the organization's own desks grant (the full form) on the same gate. One value, so there is one thing to follow. When it is absent, revoked or expired, a follow grant allows nothing.

requires_role.description: As in the full form: the organization role a run must have been started by for Govern to sign a token from this grant.
